title: Eg-walker: A Fast, Memory-Efficient Collaborative Editing Algorithm for Distributed Systems
venue: IEEE International Conference on Control, Electronics and Computer Technology (ICCECT)
abstract: Real-time collaboration features are vital in modern software, allowing multiple users to edit documents simultaneously while maintaining data integrity across devices. Traditional approaches like Operational Transformation (OT) and Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) each have limitations in handling large-scale concurrent editing and ensuring memory efficiency. In this paper, we introduce Eg-walker, a hybrid CRDT/OT algorithm that merges concurrent edits with optimal efficiency and reduced memory usage. Our evaluations show that Eg-walker can merge documents in milliseconds, requires significantly less memory than standard CRDTs, and operates effectively in peer-to-peer environments. This makes Eg-walker an efficient solution for distributed collaboration without reliance on a central server.
